note: [agent-bulk] shw 60026 (352.6 MeV, 15 seg, len 65.3, gamma1 of reco pi0 group 0) is under-clustered, and the consequence is that the reco's pi0 group looks spurious. THE MARK: 63050 (75.2 MeV, 4 seg) sits at 44.3 cm / 8.5 deg from 60026 with metric 2.9, tier 1 - strictly better on distance, angle AND metric than 60026's own accepted member 35015 (46.7 cm / 18.0 deg, metric 9.6). On the acceptance plot it is the single blue circle, and it lies INSIDE the cloud of accepted orange squares, not outside it. In the az -55 shower frame it is the compact orange fork lying straight ahead of the yellow member set along the axis arrow (I measure ~4 deg off the arrow in that projection). Marked 63050 IN. THE PI0 CLAIM: everything downstream of 60026 lines up on one axis - 63050 at 44.3 cm / 8.5 deg, its member 39019 at 70.8 / 5.8, then 38018 at 100.1 / 7.7 (tier 2), 33013 at 113.8 / 9.6 (tier 2), 18006 at 130.3 / 11.7. Both pi0 frames show it directly: in az +35 the whole thing is ONE narrow vertical column rising out of the magenta vertex star - shower core, then a chain of blobs, then the red gamma2 diamond at the top - and in az -55 the blue and red diamonds are 6.1 deg apart as seen from the vertex, matching the display's vertex-convention theta of 6.6 deg. A 6.6 deg opening with E1 352.6 and E2 20.2 gives m = 9.6 MeV; the axis convention gives 50.9 MeV; the reco stored 118.5 MeV for group 0. None of these is a pi0, and a real 135 MeV pi0 at these energies needs ~105 deg. So group 0 = 60026 + 38018 reads as a shower paired with its own downstream fragment, not as two photons. I marked 38018 IN as well, but it is the WEAKER of the two marks - tier 2 at 100 cm, past the pass-1 box, and I did not verify 3-D contiguity across the gap; 63050 is the one I would defend. Not looked at: the other 6 showers, all at or below 16.6 MeV (scope rule min_kine_best 20 MeV); shw 63050's own completeness I did not judge separately since my claim is that it is not a separate shower.
